nodes.name: Shapes in different categories can share attributes
nodes.statement: Two shapes with different category names can have an attribute in common, such as having four sides; sharing an attribute does not make them the same kind of shape.
nodes.assess: A rhombus with no right angles and a rectangle that is not a square are shown. Name one attribute both shapes have.

proposed_edges.rationale: The statement treats an attribute such as having four sides as a defining attribute that two named shapes can have in common.
Finding an attribute two different shapes have in common is done by comparing the two shapes part by part.
To say two shapes share an attribute, the learner must pick out which shapes have a given attribute.
The test problem shows a rectangle that is not a square, and the learner must know its four right angles to find what it shares.
The test problem shows a rhombus, and the learner must know its four equal sides to find what it shares.
The test problem is answered by counting the sides of the rhombus and the rectangle and noting both have four.

nodes.name: A shared attribute can define a larger category
nodes.statement: An attribute can define a category of shapes: every shape that has the attribute belongs to the category, whatever its other attributes, size, or orientation.
nodes.assess: A 'quad-shape' is any closed shape made of four straight sides. Which of these are quad-shapes: a square, a tilted kite, a rhombus, a four-sided arrowhead with one corner pointing in, a circle, a pentagon?

proposed_edges.rationale: The statement says membership holds whatever the shape's other attributes, size, or orientation, which are non-defining.
A category defined by an attribute collects shapes of different named kinds that share that one attribute.
The test problem asks the learner to pick out which listed shapes have the stated four-straight-sides attribute.

nodes.name: Recognize quadrilaterals of any shape
nodes.statement: A quadrilateral is a closed figure made of exactly four straight sides; every such figure is a quadrilateral, including irregular, tilted, and inward-pointing ones.
nodes.assess: Circle every quadrilateral: a square, a tilted kite, a four-sided arrowhead with one corner pointing in, a trapezoid, a pentagon, a figure with three straight sides and one curved side.

proposed_edges.rationale: The statement includes irregular, tilted, and inward-pointing figures, so size and orientation must not decide the name.
The statement requires a closed figure, so the test problem rejects a figure whose boundary does not close in straight sides.
A quadrilateral is the polygon named by having exactly four sides, which this node extends to any shape.

nodes.name: A rectangle is a quadrilateral with four right angles
nodes.statement: A rectangle is a quadrilateral with four right angles; its side lengths play no part in the definition.
nodes.assess: Which of these quadrilaterals are rectangles? A has four right angles and sides 2, 7, 2, 7 cm; B has four right angles and all sides 5 cm; C has sides 2, 7, 2, 7 cm and no right angles.

proposed_edges.rationale: The defining attribute of a rectangle is that all four of its angles are right angles.
The statement says side lengths play no part, which uses the idea of the attributes that define a named shape.
The definition names the rectangle as a quadrilateral, the figure with exactly four straight sides.

nodes.name: A rhombus is a quadrilateral with four equal sides
nodes.statement: A rhombus is a quadrilateral whose four sides all have the same length; its angles play no part in the definition.
nodes.assess: Which of these quadrilaterals are rhombuses? A has four sides of 5 cm and no right angles; B has four sides of 5 cm and four right angles; C has sides 5, 3, 5, 3 cm.

proposed_edges.rationale: The statement says angles play no part, which uses the idea of the attributes that define a named shape.
The defining attribute of a rhombus is that all four sides are equal in length.
The definition names the rhombus as a quadrilateral, the figure with exactly four straight sides.

nodes.name: A square has four equal sides and four right angles
nodes.statement: A square is a quadrilateral with four sides of the same length and four right angles, in any orientation.
nodes.assess: Which of these are squares? A has four sides of 4 cm and four right angles; B has four sides of 4 cm and no right angles; C has four right angles and sides 4, 6, 4, 6 cm; D is A turned to stand on one corner.

proposed_edges.rationale: A square must have four right angles, so a right angle must be recognized as a square corner.
A square must have four sides of the same length, which is the equal-sides attribute.
The statement says a square stays a square in any orientation, such as standing on a corner.
The definition names the square as a quadrilateral, the figure with exactly four straight sides.

nodes.name: Rhombuses, rectangles, and squares are quadrilaterals
nodes.statement: Rhombuses, rectangles, and squares are all quadrilaterals, because each is a closed figure with four straight sides; a shape keeps its more specific name and also belongs to the category quadrilateral.
nodes.assess: Is a square a quadrilateral? Is a rhombus? Is a rectangle? Name the attribute that decides it.

proposed_edges.rationale: A shape that has the category attribute belongs to the category while keeping its own more specific name.
The attribute that decides membership is exactly four straight sides, which defines a quadrilateral of any shape.
The statement applies the definition of a rectangle to show it is a closed figure with four straight sides.
The statement applies the definition of a rhombus to show it is a closed figure with four straight sides.
The statement applies the definition of a square to show it is a closed figure with four straight sides.

nodes.name: Draw a quadrilateral that is not a rhombus, rectangle, or square
nodes.statement: Draw a quadrilateral whose sides are not all the same length and whose angles are not all right angles, so it fits none of the definitions of rhombus, rectangle, or square.
nodes.assess: Draw a quadrilateral that is not a rhombus, not a rectangle, and not a square. Say why it is none of them.
procedure: Draw four straight sides that close into a figure.
Make at least two of the sides different in length, so it is not a rhombus or a square.
Make at least one angle that is not a right angle, so it is not a rectangle or a square.
Check the figure against each of the three definitions.

proposed_edges.rationale: Step 1 requires drawing a closed shape with four straight sides, a shape with a given number of sides.
The statement asks for a quadrilateral, so the learner must know what counts as one.
Step 3 makes one angle not right so that the figure fails the four-right-angles condition of a rectangle.
Step 2 makes two sides unequal so that the figure fails the equal-sides condition of a rhombus.
Step 4 checks the figure against the square definition of four equal sides and four right angles.

nodes.name: A point is an exact location
nodes.statement: A point is an exact location with no size, drawn as a dot and named with a capital letter; the corners of a figure are points.
nodes.assess: Draw a point on each corner of this triangle and label the points A, B, and C.

proposed_edges.rationale: The statement says the corners of a figure are points, so the learner must identify the corners of a shape.

nodes.name: A line is straight and extends without end both ways
nodes.statement: A line is straight, has no endpoints, and extends without end in both directions; it is drawn with an arrowhead at each end and named by two of its points.
nodes.assess: Which of these figures are lines: a straight path with arrowheads at both ends, a straight path with two endpoints, a straight path with one endpoint and one arrowhead, a curved path with arrowheads at both ends?

proposed_edges.rationale: A line is named by two of its points, so the learner must know what a point is.

nodes.name: A line segment is the part of a line between two endpoints
nodes.statement: A line segment is the straight part of a line between two endpoints, including them; it is named by its endpoints, and the sides of a polygon are line segments.
nodes.assess: This pentagon has points A, B, C, D, and E at its corners. Name the five line segments that form its sides.

proposed_edges.rationale: A segment is defined as the straight part of a line, so the meaning of a line is used.
A segment is bounded by two endpoints and named by them, and endpoints are points.
The statement identifies the sides of a polygon as segments, so the learner must identify sides of a shape.

nodes.name: A ray starts at an endpoint and extends without end one way
nodes.statement: A ray is the part of a line that starts at one endpoint and extends without end in one direction; it is drawn with one endpoint and one arrowhead and named starting with its endpoint.
nodes.assess: Which of these figures are rays: a straight path with one endpoint and one arrowhead, a straight path with arrowheads at both ends, a straight path with two endpoints, a curved path with one endpoint and one arrowhead?

proposed_edges.rationale: A ray is defined as the part of a line that goes on without end in one direction.
A ray starts at one endpoint and is named starting with that endpoint, which is a point.

nodes.name: A right angle forms a square corner
nodes.statement: A right angle is an angle whose two sides form a square corner, so the corner of a sheet of paper fits it exactly.
nodes.assess: Use the corner of an index card to test each angle of this quadrilateral, which is not a rectangle. Which of its angles are right angles?

proposed_edges.rationale: A right angle is a kind of angle, two rays from a common endpoint, whose sides form a square corner.
The statement describes the right angle as a square corner that fits the corner of a sheet of paper.

nodes.name: Acute and obtuse angles compared with a right angle
nodes.statement: An acute angle is smaller than a right angle; an obtuse angle is larger than a right angle and smaller than a straight angle.
nodes.assess: Label each angle of this pentagon as right, acute, or obtuse.

proposed_edges.rationale: Acute and obtuse angles are defined by comparing their opening with the square corner of a right angle.
An obtuse angle must be smaller than a straight angle, whose two sides form a straight line.

nodes.name: Draw a right, acute, or obtuse angle
nodes.statement: Draw an angle of a named type by drawing two rays from a common endpoint and checking the opening against a square corner.
nodes.assess: Draw an obtuse angle with its vertex at point P.
procedure: Draw a ray.
Place a square corner at the ray's endpoint with one edge along the ray.
For a right angle, draw the second ray along the other edge of the square corner.
For an acute angle, draw the second ray from the endpoint inside the square corner.
For an obtuse angle, draw the second ray from the endpoint between the other edge of the square corner and the extension of the first ray backward through its endpoint.

proposed_edges.rationale: Steps 4 and 5 place the second ray inside or beyond the square corner according to the acute or obtuse comparison.
The statement defines the drawn angle as two rays from a common endpoint.
Step 2 places a square corner at the endpoint, and step 3 draws the right angle along its edge.
Step 1 draws a ray, and later steps draw further rays from the same endpoint.

nodes.name: Perpendicular lines meet at right angles
nodes.statement: Two lines are perpendicular when they meet to form right angles; two segments or sides are perpendicular when the lines they lie on are perpendicular.
nodes.assess: In this trapezoid with two right angles, name every pair of sides that are perpendicular.

proposed_edges.rationale: Two lines are perpendicular when the angles they form at the meeting point are right angles.
Perpendicularity is defined as a relationship between two lines that meet.
The statement extends the idea to segments and sides, which are perpendicular when the lines they lie on are.

nodes.name: Draw a line perpendicular to a given line
nodes.statement: Draw a line perpendicular to a given line through a given point on it, using a square corner.
nodes.assess: Draw a line perpendicular to line m through the point P on m.
procedure: Place a square corner with its vertex at the point and one edge along the given line.
Draw along the other edge of the square corner, through the point.
Extend the drawn line in both directions.

proposed_edges.rationale: Step 1 uses a square corner to produce the right angle at the given point.
Step 3 extends the drawn edge in both directions so that it becomes a line.
The drawn line must satisfy the definition of being perpendicular to the given line.
Step 1 places the vertex of the square corner at the given point on the line.

nodes.name: Parallel lines never meet
nodes.statement: Two lines in a plane are parallel when they never meet, however far they are extended; two segments or sides are parallel when the lines they lie on are parallel.
nodes.assess: In this trapezoid, which has exactly one pair of parallel sides, name the pair of sides that are parallel.

proposed_edges.rationale: Parallel lines are lines that never meet however far they are extended in both directions without end.
The statement extends parallelism to segments and sides, which are parallel when their lines are.

nodes.name: Draw a line parallel to a given line
nodes.statement: Draw a line through a given point, not on a given line, that is parallel to the given line.
nodes.assess: Draw a line through point P that is parallel to line m.
procedure: Slide a square corner along the given line, one edge on the line, until its other edge passes through the point; draw along that edge.
At the point, draw a line perpendicular to the line just drawn.
The second line is parallel to the given line, because two lines perpendicular to the same line never meet.

proposed_edges.rationale: Step 1 slides a square corner along the line to draw a line at right angles to it.
The drawn line must satisfy the definition of never meeting the given line.
Step 2 draws a line perpendicular, through the point, to the line drawn in step 1.
Step 3 explains the result because two lines perpendicular to the same line never meet.

nodes.name: Sort figures by parallel or perpendicular sides
nodes.statement: Sort two-dimensional figures by whether they have at least one pair of parallel sides, or by whether they have at least one pair of perpendicular sides.
nodes.assess: Sort these six figures into two groups: those with at least one pair of perpendicular sides and those with none.
procedure: For each figure, check each pair of sides for the named relationship.
Put the figures with at least one such pair in one group and the figures with none in the other.

proposed_edges.rationale: Step 2 puts the figures with the named relationship in one group and the others in a second group.
Step 1 checks each pair of sides to see whether the lines they lie on are parallel.
Step 1 checks each pair of sides to see whether they meet at right angles.

nodes.name: Sort figures by angles of a named type
nodes.statement: Sort two-dimensional figures by whether they have at least one angle of a named type: right, acute, or obtuse.
nodes.assess: Sort these six figures into two groups: those with at least one obtuse angle and those with none.
procedure: For each figure, decide the type of each of its angles.
Put the figures with at least one angle of the named type in one group and the figures with none in the other.

proposed_edges.rationale: Step 1 also decides whether each angle is acute or obtuse compared with a right angle.
Step 1 decides for each angle whether it is a right angle by comparing with a square corner.
Step 2 puts figures with an angle of the named type in one group and the others in another.

nodes.name: Right triangles as a category
nodes.statement: A right triangle is a triangle with a right angle; right triangles form a category whatever their size, side lengths, or orientation.
nodes.assess: Which of these triangles, drawn at different sizes and turned different ways with no angle marks, are right triangles?

proposed_edges.rationale: A right triangle is defined as a triangle with a right angle, a square corner.
The statement says the category holds whatever the size or orientation, as in the turned triangles of the test problem.
The statement says right triangles form a category because they share the attribute of a right angle.
The category is a kind of triangle, the polygon named by having exactly three sides.

nodes.name: A line of symmetry folds a figure into matching parts
nodes.statement: A line of symmetry of a figure is a line across it such that folding the figure along the line makes the two parts match exactly; a figure with such a line is line-symmetric.
nodes.assess: A rectangle that is not a square has a dashed line drawn along one diagonal. Is the dashed line a line of symmetry? Explain by what happens when the rectangle is folded along it.

proposed_edges.rationale: A line of symmetry is a line across the figure along which the figure is folded.
Matching exactly means the two parts, compared as whole shapes, are the same shape and size.
The test problem uses a rectangle that is not a square, so the learner must know what a rectangle is.
Folding along the line flips one part over onto the other part.

nodes.name: Draw all lines of symmetry of a figure
nodes.statement: Find and draw every line of symmetry of a two-dimensional figure; for a polygon the candidate lines can be listed in full.
nodes.assess: Draw every line of symmetry of this rectangle that is not a square.
procedure: List the candidate lines. For a polygon, every line of symmetry passes through two points that are each a vertex or the midpoint of a side, so the candidates are the lines through two such points.
For each candidate, check whether folding along it makes the two parts match exactly.
Draw every candidate that passes, and no others.

proposed_edges.rationale: Step 1 forms candidate lines through two points and step 3 draws the lines that pass.
Step 1 requires locating the midpoint of each side, which splits the side into two equal lengths.
Step 1 picks out vertices and midpoints of sides as points through which candidate lines pass.
Step 1 uses the sides of a polygon, which are segments, to find their midpoints.
The test problem asks for the lines of symmetry of a rectangle, so its vertices and sides must be known.
The procedure lists candidate lines and checks each one against the definition of a line of symmetry.

nodes.name: Axes and origin of a coordinate plane
nodes.statement: A coordinate plane is made from two perpendicular number lines, the axes (the x-axis and the y-axis), placed so they cross at 0 on each; the crossing point is the origin, with coordinates (0, 0).
nodes.assess: On this grid with both axes drawn and numbered, mark the origin and write its coordinates.

proposed_edges.rationale: The statement writes the origin in the pair notation (0, 0).
Each axis is a number line, with whole numbers marked as lengths from 0.
The two axes are defined as perpendicular number lines that meet at right angles.

nodes.name: The two coordinates as distances from the origin
nodes.statement: In an ordered pair (a, b), the first number a tells how far to travel from the origin in the direction of the x-axis, and the second number b tells how far to travel in the direction of the y-axis; so (a, b) and (b, a) are different points unless a = b.
nodes.assess: Without plotting, describe how to travel from the origin to (2, 6) and how to travel from the origin to (6, 2). Are they the same point?

proposed_edges.rationale: The coordinates tell how far to travel from the origin along the x-axis and y-axis.
The statement is about the order of the two numbers in the pair (a, b).
Each coordinate is a distance measured as a length from 0 along one axis.

nodes.name: Plot a point with whole-number coordinates in the first quadrant
nodes.statement: Plot the point with given whole-number coordinates (a, b) on a first-quadrant coordinate grid.
nodes.assess: Plot the points (5, 2) and (0, 3) on this grid.
procedure: Start at the origin.
Move a units in the direction of the x-axis.
From there, move b units in the direction of the y-axis.
Mark the point reached.

proposed_edges.rationale: Step 1 starts at the origin, the crossing point of the two axes.
Steps 2 and 3 move a units along the x-axis then b units in the y direction, as the pair tells.
The given point is written as an ordered pair (a, b) whose parts must be read in order.
Step 4 marks the point reached, an exact location drawn as a dot.

nodes.name: Read the coordinates of a point in the first quadrant
nodes.statement: Give the ordered pair of whole-number coordinates of a point plotted on a first-quadrant coordinate grid.
nodes.assess: Write the ordered pair for each of the unlabeled plotted points A and B on this grid; A lies on the y-axis.
procedure: From the point, follow the grid line parallel to the y-axis to the x-axis; the number there is the x-coordinate.
From the point, follow the grid line parallel to the x-axis to the y-axis; the number there is the y-coordinate.
Write the pair as (x-coordinate, y-coordinate).

proposed_edges.rationale: Steps 1 and 2 read numbers on the x-axis and y-axis, which must be identified.
Steps 1 and 2 name the first number the x-coordinate and the second the y-coordinate.
Step 3 writes the two coordinates as an ordered pair with the x-coordinate first.
Steps 1 and 2 follow the grid line parallel to one axis from the point to the other axis.

nodes.name: Solve a mathematical problem by graphing points
nodes.statement: Solve a mathematical problem by graphing points in the first quadrant and reasoning from their positions, such as finding a missing vertex of a figure.
nodes.assess: Three corners of a rectangle are at (1, 2), (1, 6), and (5, 6). Plot them and find the coordinates of the fourth corner.

proposed_edges.rationale: The statement requires graphing the given points in the first quadrant.
The test problem asks for the coordinates of the fourth corner after finding its position on the grid.
The fourth corner is found by using the right angles and sides of the rectangle formed by the three given corners.

nodes.name: Graph paired quantities from a real-world situation
nodes.statement: Represent a real-world situation that pairs two quantities by graphing each pair as a point in the first quadrant, the first quantity along the x-axis and the second along the y-axis.
nodes.assess: A plant was 2 cm tall at week 0, 4 cm at week 1, 6 cm at week 2, and 8 cm at week 3. Graph these as points with weeks on the x-axis and height in centimeters on the y-axis.

proposed_edges.rationale: Each pair of quantities is graphed as a point in the first quadrant.
The first quantity goes along the x-axis and the second along the y-axis, as in an ordered pair.

nodes.name: Interpret coordinate values in context
nodes.statement: Say what each coordinate of a plotted point means in the situation the graph represents.
nodes.assess: A graph shows hours worked on the x-axis and dollars earned on the y-axis. The point (3, 24) is plotted. What do the 3 and the 24 tell you?

proposed_edges.rationale: Saying what each coordinate means uses the first number as the x distance and the second as the y distance.

nodes.name: Trapezoids and parallelograms by pairs of parallel sides
nodes.statement: A trapezoid is a quadrilateral with at least one pair of parallel sides; a parallelogram is a quadrilateral with two pairs of parallel sides.
nodes.assess: Quadrilateral A has exactly one pair of parallel sides, B has two pairs, and C has none. Which of A, B, and C are trapezoids? Which are parallelograms?

proposed_edges.rationale: The definitions count the pairs of parallel sides, so parallel must be known.
Trapezoids and parallelograms are defined as kinds of quadrilateral, the figures with four straight sides.

nodes.name: Equilateral, isosceles, and scalene triangles
nodes.statement: An equilateral triangle has three sides of equal length; an isosceles triangle has at least two sides of equal length; a scalene triangle has no two sides of equal length.
nodes.assess: Three triangles have sides 5, 5, 5 cm; 5, 5, 8 cm; and 4, 6, 7 cm. Which are isosceles? Which are scalene?

proposed_edges.rationale: Each category is defined by how many sides of the triangle are equal in length.
These categories are kinds of triangle, the polygon named by having exactly three sides.

nodes.name: Acute, right, and obtuse triangles
nodes.statement: An acute triangle has three acute angles; a right triangle has a right angle; an obtuse triangle has an obtuse angle.
nodes.assess: Name each of these three triangles, drawn with no angle marks, as acute, right, or obtuse.

proposed_edges.rationale: Acute and obtuse triangles are defined by whether their angles are acute or obtuse.
A right triangle is defined as a triangle that has a right angle.
These categories are kinds of triangle, the polygon named by having exactly three sides.

nodes.name: Attributes of a category belong to all its subcategories
nodes.statement: If every shape in a category has an attribute, then every shape in each subcategory of that category has the attribute too.
nodes.assess: All parallelograms have diagonals that cut each other in half. Every rhombus is a parallelogram. Without measuring, must the diagonals of every rhombus cut each other in half? Explain using the categories.

proposed_edges.rationale: A subcategory is a category whose members also have the attribute that defines the larger category.
The test problem relies on a rhombus belonging to the larger category of parallelograms while keeping its own name.

nodes.name: Name every category a quadrilateral belongs to
nodes.statement: Name every category among trapezoid, parallelogram, rectangle, rhombus, and square that a given quadrilateral belongs to, by checking its parallel sides, right angles, and side lengths against each definition.
nodes.assess: A quadrilateral has four sides of 6 cm and four right angles. List every name it has among trapezoid, parallelogram, rectangle, rhombus, and square.
procedure: Count the pairs of parallel sides; at least one pair makes it a trapezoid, two pairs make it a parallelogram.
Check the angles; four right angles (each pair of adjacent sides perpendicular) make it a rectangle.
Check the side lengths; four equal sides make it a rhombus.
Four equal sides and four right angles make it a square.
List every name whose condition holds.

proposed_edges.rationale: Step 1 counts the pairs of parallel sides of the quadrilateral.
Step 2 treats each pair of adjacent sides at a right angle as perpendicular.
Step 5 lists every name whose attribute holds, since a shape belongs to every category it has the attribute of.
Step 1 applies the definitions: one pair makes a trapezoid, two pairs make a parallelogram.
Step 2 checks the definition of a rectangle, four right angles.
Step 3 checks the definition of a rhombus, four equal sides.
Step 4 checks the definition of a square, four equal sides and four right angles.

nodes.name: The hierarchy of quadrilateral categories
nodes.statement: The quadrilateral categories are nested by inclusion: every square is both a rectangle and a rhombus, every rectangle and every rhombus is a parallelogram, every parallelogram is a trapezoid, and every trapezoid is a quadrilateral.
nodes.assess: True or false, with a reason from the definitions: every square is a rhombus; every rhombus is a square; every rectangle is a parallelogram.

proposed_edges.rationale: A rectangle's opposite sides are parallel because adjacent sides are perpendicular to the same line.
Nesting by inclusion means each smaller category is the set of shapes with the extra defining attributes.
The reasons from definitions in the test problem apply the same condition checks that naming every category of a quadrilateral uses.
Rectangles and rhombuses are parallelograms, and parallelograms trapezoids, by the parallel-sides definitions.
Inclusion of the square and the rectangle in other categories is shown from the definition of a rectangle.
Inclusion of the square and the rhombus in other categories is shown from the definition of a rhombus.
Every square is both a rectangle and a rhombus because its definition contains both sets of conditions.

nodes.name: The hierarchy of triangle categories
nodes.statement: Equilateral triangles are a subcategory of isosceles triangles, and the categories by sides cross the categories by angles, so one triangle can belong to both kinds, such as an isosceles right triangle.
nodes.assess: True or false, with a reason from the definitions: every equilateral triangle is isosceles; every isosceles triangle is equilateral; a right triangle can be isosceles.

proposed_edges.rationale: A triangle that has the attribute of each category belongs to both, so categories can cross or nest.
The crossing of categories by sides with categories by angles uses the definitions by angles.
The nesting of equilateral inside isosceles follows from the definitions of the categories by sides.
